court_name: Small claims court (District Court, cases heard by a magistrate)
limit_notes: Up to $10,000 (G.S. 7A-210, limit set in 2013). Relief must be money, recovery of specific personal property, or summary ejectment (eviction). The plaintiff must request assignment to a magistrate, and the case is filed in the county where a defendant resides.
filing_fee_notes: $96 total for a case assigned to a magistrate (G.S. 7A-305(a)): $80 General Court of Justice fee + $12 facilities fee + $4 court technology fee. Sheriff service is $30 per defendant (G.S. 7A-311); certified mail costs postage. Counterclaims pay the same costs (7A-305(a5)).
who_can_sue: Individuals and organizations may sue. A business may be represented in small claims by a non-lawyer authorized agent, such as an owner or employee.
lawyers_notes: Parties may use attorneys; not required.
appeal: Either party may appeal for a trial de novo before a district court judge or jury (G.S. 7A-228). Notice may be given orally in open court, or in writing to the clerk within 10 days after judgment. Appeal costs must be paid within 20 days (10 days for summary ejectment) or the appeal is dismissed. Indigent appeal is available by affidavit within 10 days.
e_filing_notes: eCourts runs in all 100 counties (since Oct. 13, 2025). Self-represented people can e-file through File & Serve (optional for them) or use the free Guide & File interview for small claims money-owed and personal-property cases. Paper filing at the clerk of superior court is still allowed.
fee_waiver_form: Petition to Proceed as an Indigent (AOC-G-106): https://www.nccourts.gov/documents/forms/petition-to-proceed-as-an-indigent
fee_waiver_threshold: The clerk must grant on affidavit if the person receives SNAP (food and nutrition benefits), Work First, or SSI, or is represented by legal services. A judge or clerk may also grant it to others unable to advance costs (G.S. 1-110).
service_methods: Personal delivery or substitute service at the dwelling (usually by sheriff); registered or certified mail, signature confirmation, or designated delivery service; acceptance of service (G.S. 7A-217).
citation: N.C. Gen. Stat. §§ 7A-210 to 7A-232; § 7A-305 (costs); § 7A-311 (service fees); § 1-110 (indigency)

court_name: Small claims court (district court judges or appointed referees)
limit_notes: Money claims, tenant mobile-home-park damages under 47-10-28(9), or cancellation of an agreement for fraud or misrepresentation, up to $15,000 (N.D.C.C. 27-08.1-01). Counterclaims are also capped at $15,000. Venue rules depend on the defendant type. Except for certain claims, the defendant may move the case to the small claims court of the defendant's home county. No jury trials.
filing_fee_notes: $20 for filing a small claims action (N.D.C.C. 27-05.2-03(1)(e)). Section 27-08.1-03 still cross-references the old subdivision (c), which is a drafting mismatch. Service costs (certified mail or process server) are extra. A defendant who removes the case to district court pays the regular civil filing fee.
who_can_sue: Any person, including businesses. Assigned claims may not be filed (so no collection agencies or debt buyers) (27-08.1-01(3)).
lawyers_notes: Parties 'may appear without counsel' (27-08.1-03); attorneys are not prohibited. If a defendant removes the case to district court and the plaintiff wins, the court must award the plaintiff attorney's fees.
appeal: No appeal. By choosing small claims, the plaintiff waives appeal. The defendant waives appeal on receiving the order for appearance unless the defendant removes the case to district court, within 20 days of service, before the hearing (27-08.1-04). The court's page says small claims decisions are final.
e_filing_notes: District courts use the Odyssey e-filing system statewide. Self-represented people don't have to e-file (paper in person, by mail or by carrier is fine) but may choose to e-file through Odyssey (N.D.R.Ct. 3.5). Rule 3.5 doesn't mention small claims specifically.
fee_waiver_form: Petition for Waiver of Filing Fees (Form 1) plus Financial Declaration in Support (Form 2), from the ND Legal Self Help Center, usable for small claims (N.D.C.C. § 27-01-07): https://www.ndcourts.gov/Media/Default/Legal%20Resources/Legal%20Self%20Help/Other%20Forms/Fee%20Waiver/All%20Petition%20for%20Fee%20Waiver%20Instructions%20%20Forms.pdf
fee_waiver_threshold: No fixed income test. The judge or judicial referee decides based on a financial declaration (public assistance received, income, expenses, assets). The waiver covers the filing fee only, not service, copy or transcript costs.
service_methods: The plaintiff serves the claim affidavit and forms by a non-party adult (personal service) or by certified mail with restricted delivery, anywhere in the state (27-08.1-02). The defendant has 20 days to request a hearing or remove the case to district court, or a default may be entered.

court_name: Small claims division of municipal and county courts
limit_notes: Recovery of money or taxes up to $6,000 excluding interest and costs (R.C. 1925.02(A)(1)). Excluded: libel, slander, replevin, malicious prosecution, abuse of process, punitive damages, and claims by an assignee or agent (with exceptions for tax claims and certain holders of retail installment contracts). Counterclaims over $6,000 move the case to the regular docket.
recent_changes: R.C. 1925.02 amended by S.B. 237 (135th G.A.), effective April 9, 2025, adjusting the assignee exceptions for holders of security agreements and retail installment contracts. The $6,000 limit is unchanged since H.B. 387 (2016).
filing_fee_notes: Each court sets its own fee (R.C. 1925.04). Examples: Sandusky Municipal Court $105 (one or two defendants, +$10 each additional), personal service $35. Franklin County Municipal Court announced a $6 small claims cost increase in June 2026; bailiff service $25 per defendant. Certified mail service is usually included or billed by the clerk.
who_can_sue: Individuals and businesses. Assignees and agents generally cannot sue (no collection agencies). A corporation may sue through an attorney, or through a bona fide officer or salaried employee on claims where it was the original party. Non-attorney corporate representatives may not cross-examine or argue (R.C. 1925.17).
lawyers_notes: Attorneys may appear for any party. Non-attorney corporate representatives are limited (see who_can_sue).
appeal: Small claims cases are usually heard by a magistrate. Either party may file written objections to the magistrate's decision within 14 days of its filing (another party may then object within 10 days after the first objections); objecting to findings of fact requires a transcript (Civ.R. 53(D)(3)(b)). The judge then rules and enters judgment. Either party may appeal the final judgment to the district court of appeals by filing a notice of appeal within 30 days of entry of the judgment (App.R. 4(A)); review is on the record, not a new trial. Failing to object to the magistrate's decision generally limits what can be raised on appeal.
e_filing_notes: Ohio has no statewide trial-court e-filing. Some municipal courts let self-represented people e-file (e.g., Findlay Municipal Court); others, such as Franklin County Municipal Court, take small claims at the clerk's office. Check the local court.
fee_waiver_form: Affidavit of indigency in the Supreme Court-approved form (R.C. 2323.311): Form 20, Civil Fee Waiver Affidavit and Order, https://www.supremecourt.ohio.gov/docs/JCS/courtSvcs/justiceAccess/resources/CivilFeeWaiver.pdf. Many courts post their own copy.
fee_waiver_threshold: Approved if household gross income is at or below 187.5% of the federal poverty guidelines and monthly expenses are at least equal to liquid assets; a judge may also approve someone above these limits (R.C. 2323.311, applied to municipal courts by R.C. 1901.26).
service_methods: Notice served under the Civil Rules (R.C. 1925.05), usually by certified mail from the clerk. If that fails: personal service by bailiff or sheriff, or ordinary mail after certified mail is refused or unclaimed. Published service cannot be used (R.C. 1925.02(A)(3)).
citation: Ohio Rev. Code ch. 1925 (§§ 1925.01-1925.18); Ohio Civ.R. 53; App.R. 4

court_name: Small claims docket of the District Court
limit_notes: Money claims (contract or tort, including subrogation; not libel or slander), replevin of property, and interpleader up to $10,000 excluding attorney fees and costs (12 O.S. 1751(A)). No claims by collection agencies, collection agents or assignees (narrow exception for health care providers suing insurers). No claims by incarcerated plaintiffs, or against government agencies about incarceration or supervision. The affidavit must include a jury-trial waiver statement.
recent_changes: HB 1611 (2024, c. 108), effective Nov. 1, 2024, lets corporations, LLCs, partnerships, trusts and other entities appear through an officer, member, manager, partner, trustee or regular full-time employee. HB 1129 (2025), which would have raised the small claims fee, failed in the House on March 12, 2025. The current AOC fee schedule is effective Nov. 1, 2025.
filing_fee_notes: Affidavit fee: $45 for claims of $5,000 or less; $150 for $5,000-$10,000 (12 O.S. 1764; AOC schedule effective 11/1/2025). Add-ons push the actual total higher: an Oklahoma County docket shows $45 + $7 dispute mediation + $6 law library = $58. Plus mailing ($10 per person, or actual cost) or sheriff service ($50 per person). Transfer to another docket: $50.
who_can_sue: Individuals and entities, but not collection agencies or assignees. Since Nov. 1, 2024, entities may appear through an officer, member, manager, partner, trustee or regular full-time employee (12 O.S. 1751(G)). Incarcerated persons may not sue.
lawyers_notes: Attorneys may appear. In uncontested cases attorney fees are capped at 10% of the judgment (up to 25% on application) (12 O.S. 1751(C)).
appeal: Appeals go to the Oklahoma Supreme Court in the same manner as other civil appeals (12 O.S. 1763), i.e. on the record by petition in error, generally within 30 days of the filed judgment.
e_filing_notes: E-filing through OSCN (OUCMS) works in district courts county by county as the system is rolled out. Self-represented people may e-file in their own case after registering on efile.oscn.net but don't have to (Okla. E-Filing Rules 1, 10). Small claims aren't mentioned separately; paper filing with the court clerk is still available.
fee_waiver_form: Affidavit in forma pauperis (pauper's affidavit), sworn before a notary or other officer (28 O.S. § 152(H); statutory form at 12 O.S. § 922). No statewide court-published form.
fee_waiver_threshold: No income test. The court holds a hearing and decides whether, because of poverty, you can't pay the fees and costs; the other side can contest it with its own affidavit. Until the court rules, the clerk must let the case go forward without fees (28 O.S. § 152(H)).
service_methods: By default, the clerk mails the affidavit and order by certified mail, restricted to the addressee, return receipt. If it comes back undelivered, the sheriff serves. Or the plaintiff may elect service under 12 O.S. 2004(C) (sheriff or licensed process server) (12 O.S. 1755).
citation: Okla. Stat. tit. 12, §§ 1751-1773 (Small Claims Procedure Act); tit. 28, §§ 152, 152.1 (fees)

court_name: Small claims department of the circuit court (some justice courts also hear small claims)
limit_notes: Claims for money, damages, specific personal property, or a penalty or forfeiture up to $10,000. Claims of $750 or less MUST be filed in small claims (with exceptions, e.g. statutory attorney-fee claims). Class actions are not allowed, nor are suits by one adult in custody against another (ORS 46.405). Where a justice court operates in the same city under an intergovernmental agreement, small claims may be handled by the justice court instead.
filing_fee_notes: $57 for claims of $2,500 or less; $102 for claims over $2,500 (ORS 46.570). A defendant demanding a hearing pays the same fee. Sheriff service is $45 (ORS 21.300); certified mail costs postage.
who_can_sue: Individuals and entities. Non-natural persons and public bodies may appear without an attorney (ORS 46.415(5)). Assignees may sue to the same extent as in other state courts (ORS 46.415(6)). One spouse may appear for both with consent.
lawyers_notes: No attorney (or anyone other than the parties) may appear for a party without the judge's consent (ORS 46.415(4)). If the claim is over $750, the defendant may demand a jury trial; the case then moves to the regular circuit court, where lawyers may appear.
appeal: No appeal: a small claims judgment is conclusive (ORS 46.485(4)). A defendant who wants a jury trial (claims over $750) must demand it within 30 days of service, instead of a small claims hearing. A default judgment may be set aside for good cause within 60 days.
e_filing_notes: OJD eFile is available in all circuit courts, including to self-represented litigants (individual accounts). OJD Guide & File prepares small claims forms. Fee waiver or deferral applications cannot be e-filed. Not confirmed that small claims are excluded under UTCR 21.070(3).
fee_waiver_form: Application for Deferral or Waiver of Fees & Declaration in Support, plus Order Regarding Deferral or Waiver of Fees (OJD statewide forms; application Feb 2022, instructions Jan 2026): https://www.courts.oregon.gov/forms/Documents/Gen-FeeWaiver-Applic-Decl.pdf . One application per fee, except the sheriff's service fee. E-filers may submit it through File & Serve.
fee_waiver_threshold: Low income according to federal poverty guidelines (no percentage stated). The application asks about legal-aid representation and public benefits (SNAP, SSI, TANF, OHP). The court may waive, defer (payment plan, possibly with collection costs), postpone ruling, or deny. A deferral or denial becomes a judgment for the fees. The clerk may decide first, and a denial can be reviewed by a judge (ORS 21.682: party 'unable to pay').
service_methods: At the plaintiff's option: certified mail ('Deliver to Addressee Only', return receipt requested) mailed by the plaintiff, or service as for a circuit court summons (sheriff, or any competent non-party adult). If certified mail fails, personal or other summons-type service is required (ORS 46.445).
citation: Or. Rev. Stat. §§ 46.405-46.570; ORS 21.300 (sheriff fees); ORS ch. 55 (justice court small claims)

court_name: Magisterial District Courts (civil actions); in Philadelphia, Philadelphia Municipal Court, Civil Division (small claims)
limit_notes: Magisterial district judges hear civil claims up to $12,000 excluding interest and costs (42 Pa.C.S. 1515(a)(3)). Philadelphia Municipal Court small claims also go up to $12,000 (42 Pa.C.S. 1123(a)(4)). Pennsylvania has no separate 'small claims court' outside Philadelphia: MDJ civil actions serve that role.
recent_changes: MDJ civil filing costs rise every Jan. 1 with CPI under Act 54 of 2024 (42 Pa.C.S. 1725.1(f)). The calendar-2026 costs are $68.50 / $91.00 / $114.00 / $171.00, up from $67 / $89 / $111.50 / $167 in 2025.
filing_fee_notes: Magisterial district courts, calendar 2026 (42 Pa.C.S. 1725.1(a)): $68.50 for claims of $500 or less; $91.00 for $500-$2,000; $114.00 for $2,000-$4,000; $171.00 for $4,001-$12,000. Postage, certified mail and constable or sheriff service are extra. Philadelphia Municipal Court: $94.75 (up to $2,000) or $116.75 ($2,000.01-$12,000) with one Philadelphia defendant served by the court; $67.75 / $89.75 without court service; plus $45 per service outside Philadelphia.
who_can_sue: Individuals (in person, through a lawyer, or through a non-lawyer representative with personal knowledge of the case and written authorization). Partnerships may appear through a partner, a lawyer, or an employee or agent with personal knowledge and written authorization. Corporations and other entities may appear through an officer, a lawyer, or an employee or agent with personal knowledge and written authorization from an officer. Authorization must be filed before the representative acts and is case by case (no blanket authorizations, no businesses set up to represent others). Minors and incapacitated persons appear through a guardian (Ch. 800). Philadelphia uses an Appointment of Authorized Representative form.
lawyers_notes: Parties may use lawyers; not required. In Philadelphia, a lawyer needn't file the authorized-representative form.
appeal: Either party aggrieved by a magisterial district judge's money judgment may appeal within 30 days after the date of entry of the judgment by filing a notice of appeal (with a copy of the Notice of Judgment) with the prothonotary of the county Court of Common Pleas; late appeals only with leave of court for good cause (Pa.R.Civ.P.M.D.J. 1002(A)). The appeal is a new trial (de novo) under the ordinary Common Pleas rules (Rule 1007(A)). Philadelphia Municipal Court money judgments are likewise appealed to the Court of Common Pleas within 30 days of entry on the docket, de novo (Phila. Civ. R. *1001 et seq.).
e_filing_notes: PACFile (UJS portal) offers e-filing for some court levels; whether MDJ civil complaints can be filed online by the public wasn't confirmed. Philadelphia Municipal Court says civil e-filing is 'not available at this time'; new small claims are filed in person (appointments preferred).
fee_waiver_form: Petition to proceed in forma pauperis (Pa.R.Civ.P.M.D.J. 206); Philadelphia Municipal Court 'Petition to Proceed In Forma Pauperis' form
fee_waiver_threshold: A party 'without financial resources to pay the costs of litigation' may proceed in forma pauperis on petition and affidavit; the MDJ rules within 5 days. Automatic if a free legal services attorney certifies (Pa.R.Civ.P.M.D.J. 206).
service_methods: MDJ: personal service by the sheriff or a certified constable (the MDJ delivers the complaint to them; a certified constable may serve anywhere in the state; outside the county, through that county's sheriff/constable or, in Philadelphia, the Municipal Court's writ server or sheriff). Or, where the rules allow and at the plaintiff's option, the court mails it by certified mail or a comparable method with a return receipt. Service must be at least 10 days before the hearing. Philadelphia Municipal Court: court service ($27 per Philadelphia address) or out-of-county sheriff ($45).
citation: 42 Pa.C.S. §§ 1515(a)(3), 1123(a)(4), 1725.1; Pa. R. Civ. P. for Magisterial District Judges 201-1013; Phila. M.C.R. Civ. P.

court_name: District Court, Small Claims (small claims procedure under R.I. Gen. Laws ch. 10-16)
limit_notes: Money only, $5,000 exclusive of interest and costs, for: contract (ex contractu) actions and tax claims; damages from a retail sale of goods or services to a member of the public; and claims on negotiable instruments (§ 10-16-1). The statute does not list ordinary tort claims, so not every kind of case fits. court_name: Magistrates Court (Summary Court), civil side; there is no separate small claims court
limit_notes: $7,500 for contract, property damage, personal injury, penalties, recovery of personal property, etc. (S.C. Code § 22-3-10). Landlord-tenant / possession cases have no dollar cap (§ 22-3-10(10), (12)). If a counterclaim would exceed $7,500 the whole case moves to the Court of Common Pleas (§ 22-3-30). Magistrates cannot hear cases where title to real estate is in question or (mostly) where the State is a party (§ 22-3-20).
recent_changes: 2026 Act No. 155 (H.4813), effective January 1, 2027: summons-and-complaint fee rises from $45 to $65 (§ 8-21-1010(A)(6)) and the filing assessment from $25 to $40 (§ 22-3-340), so the total goes from $70 to $105; execution fee $10 to $20; landlord-tenant proceedings $20 to $40. filing_fee_notes: Uniform statewide: $45 summons/complaint fee (§ 8-21-1010(A)(6)) + $25 assessment (§ 22-3-340) = $70 through December 31, 2026; $105 from January 1, 2027. Service costs (sheriff/constable, process server, or certified mail) are extra and vary by county.
who_can_sue: Individuals. A business may be represented by a non-lawyer officer, agent, or employee in civil magistrates court if it gives the court written authorization signed by its president, chair, general partner, owner, or CEO (S.C. Rules for Magistrates Court, Rule 21). Assignees/collection agencies not specifically addressed.
lawyers_notes: Parties may hire attorneys; most self-represent. Jury trial available on written request at least 5 working days before trial (Magistrates Rule 13(c), per the court FAQ).
appeal: Either party may move for a new trial within 5 days, or appeal to the Circuit Court in the county by serving a notice of appeal within 30 days after written notice of judgment (or after the judgment is announced in their presence) (S.C. fee_waiver_threshold: Magistrate's discretion on an affidavit of inability to pay (no fixed income test). If granted, filing fees are waived but other court costs remain (court FAQ); see also § 8-21-1020.
service_methods: Sheriff's department; private process server; certified mail, restricted delivery, return receipt requested (plaintiff files a notarized affidavit with the receipt); publication by court order if the others fail (Magistrates Rule 6(c), per the court FAQ). court_name: Small claims, Civil Division of the Superior Court
limit_notes: $10,000, money damages only; no slander or libel; claims may not be split (12 V.S.A. § 5531(a)-(b)). Collection of consumer credit debt or medical debt is capped at $5,000 (§ 5531(e)). Counterclaims from the same transaction may ask for more but judgment is capped at the limit (§ 5533(c)). If the claim is over $3,500 the defendant may request a Superior judge or appointed attorney to hear it (§ 5531(c)).
recent_changes: 2023 Act No. 46 (S.33), signed June 5, 2023 and effective on passage, raised the small claims limit from $5,000 to $10,000 (and the claim-splitting bar to match). The $5,000 cap on collecting consumer-credit and medical debt was kept, not added. Before that, the limit was last raised in 2007 ($3,500 to $5,000).
filing_fee_notes: $65 for claims of $1,000 or less; $90 for claims over $1,000. Counterclaim $25 ($500 or less) or $35. Jury request $10. Appeal $120. Post-judgment motion $65.
who_can_sue: Must be 18 (parent or guardian sues for a minor). Businesses may use small claims. You cannot sue on someone else's behalf; each co-plaintiff must sign and attend. Collection of consumer credit/medical debt capped at $5,000.
lawyers_notes: Any person, corporation or other entity may be, but need not be, represented by an attorney (12 V.S.A. § 5536).
appeal: Any party may appeal to the Civil Division within 30 days of the date the court issued the judgment; a different Superior judge decides on the record (audio recording and evidence), with no new evidence (12 V.S.A. § 5538; court page). No appeal as of right to the Vermont Supreme Court; only by permission.
e_filing_notes: Court page: file in person, by mail, by email, or electronically (e-file) with the Civil Division.
fee_waiver_form: Application to Waive Filing Fees and Service Costs (600-00228): https://www.vtcourts.gov/self-help/application-waive-filing-fees-and-service-costs
fee_waiver_threshold: Receives any public assistance, OR gross income at or below 150% of federal poverty guidelines, OR the court finds you cannot pay without using resources needed to support you and your dependents.
service_methods: Court mails the signed summons and complaint back to the plaintiff; plaintiff sends them to the defendant by first-class mail within 7 days and files a Certificate of Service. If no answer within 30 days, plaintiff must have a sheriff or constable serve; return of service due within 60 days of first mailing. Alternative service or publication by motion.
citation: 12 V.S.A. §§ 5531-5541; Vermont Rules of Small Claims Procedure

court_name: Small Claims Court (small claims division of the General District Court)
limit_notes: Small claims division: up to $5,000 exclusive of interest (Va. Code § 16.1-122.2), for money or recovery of personal property; counterclaims also capped at $5,000 (§ 16.1-122.3(F)). The General District Court itself is higher: exclusive jurisdiction up to $4,500 and concurrent with circuit court up to $50,000 (§ 16.1-77), so a plaintiff may instead file on the regular GDC docket (lawyers allowed there). No suits against the Commonwealth under the Tort Claims Act (§ 16.1-122.1). Defendant may remove the case to the regular GDC docket any time before decision (§ 16.1-122.4(B)).
filing_fee_notes: $36 court services fee per civil warrant (Va. Code § 16.1-69.48:2) plus local add-ons (e.g., courthouse construction fee) that vary by court; sheriff service $12 per defendant (§ 17.1-272). Use the official GDC Civil Filing Fee Calculation tool for the exact total.
who_can_sue: Parties represent themselves. A corporation, partnership, LLC or other entity may be represented by an owner, general partner, officer, member, or employee; a party who can't participate may be helped by a non-attorney friend or relative with the judge's OK (§ 16.1-122.4). Assignees not specifically addressed.
lawyers_notes: Attorneys may not represent parties in small claims court; an attorney may appear only for himself, and a defendant may use an attorney to remove the case to the regular General District Court docket (§ 16.1-122.4).
appeal: Same as other General District Court cases (§ 16.1-122.7): any party may appeal to circuit court for a new trial (de novo) if the amount in controversy exceeds $20, by noting the appeal within 10 days of judgment (§ 16.1-106) and posting bond and paying the writ tax/costs within 30 days (§ 16.1-107). No bond for a plaintiff where no counterclaim was filed, or for an indigent defendant.
e_filing_notes: Virginia's e-filing system (VJEFS) is for attorneys in circuit court only; small claims cases are filed with the GDC clerk.
fee_waiver_form: Petition for Proceeding in Civil Case Without Payment of Fees or Costs (Form DC-409, rev. 07/21; Va. Code §§ 16.1-69.48:4, 17.1-606): https://vacourts.gov/forms/district/dc409.pdf
fee_waiver_threshold: Presumed unable to pay if receiving state or federal public assistance for the indigent or represented by legal aid; otherwise the court compares available funds to 125% of federal poverty guidelines (Va. Code § 17.1-606).
service_methods: Clerk sends the warrant to the sheriff for service, or the plaintiff may use a private process server: personal, substituted (family member 16+ at home), or posting on the door. Plaintiff should also mail a copy first-class at least 10 days before trial and file Certificate of Mailing (DC-413), required before default on posted service.

court_name: Small Claims Department of the District Court
limit_notes: Money only: $10,000 for claims brought by a natural person, $5,000 for all other plaintiffs (businesses, etc.) (RCW 12.40.010). A defendant cannot remove the case by filing an oversized counterclaim; larger counterclaims may be filed separately in superior court (RCW 12.40.027).
filing_fee_notes: $35 filing fee (RCW 12.40.020) plus any county dispute-resolution-center surcharge of up to $15 (RCW 7.75.035). Same fee for counterclaims. Service fee and mileage extra (RCW 12.40.040).
who_can_sue: The real claimant only: the claim must be verified by the real claimant and NO claim may be filed or prosecuted by an assignee (RCW 12.40.070), so collection agencies/assignees cannot use small claims. Corporations appear through non-lawyer representatives (attorneys barred).
lawyers_notes: No attorney, legal paraprofessional or other person may appear without the judge's consent; a corporation may not be represented by an attorney (RCW 12.40.080), except where a district court case was transferred into small claims (RCW 12.40.025).
appeal: Either party may appeal to superior court within 30 days of judgment by filing a notice of appeal in district court, paying the superior court filing fee, posting a bond (twice the judgment or amount in controversy), and serving all parties (RCW 12.36.020). The appeal is de novo on the record (RCW 12.36.055). No appeal if the amount claimed was under $250, and a party who filed a claim for less than $1,000 cannot appeal (RCW 12.40.120; RCW 12.36.010).
e_filing_notes: Not confirmed; e-filing in district courts varies by court.
fee_waiver_form: Motion and Declaration for Waiver of Civil Fees and Surcharges (mandatory AOC pattern form under GR 34)
fee_waiver_threshold: Indigent if receiving needs-based means-tested assistance (TANF, GA-U/GA-X, SSI, poverty-related veterans benefits, food stamps), OR household income at or below 125% of federal poverty guideline, OR above 125% with basic living expenses that leave no ability to pay, OR other compelling circumstances (GR 34(a)(3)).
service_methods: Personal service as for a summons (RCW 4.28.080) or registered/certified mail with a signed return receipt filed with the court; must be complete at least 10 days before the first hearing (RCW 12.40.040).

court_name: Magistrate Court (civil); no separate small claims court
limit_notes: Civil actions up to $20,000 exclusive of interest and costs; evictions/wrongful occupation if title not in dispute (W. Va. Code § 50-2-1). No equity, eminent domain, real estate title, lien foreclosure, false imprisonment, malicious prosecution, or libel/slander cases. Removal to circuit court: for claims of $5,000 or more any party may remove before trial; under $5,000 all parties must agree (§ 50-4-8).
recent_changes: Limit raised to $20,000 by Enrolled Committee Substitute for HB 2761 (2025), passed April 8, 2025, in effect July 7, 2025 (previously $10,000 per bill summaries). Many online charts still show $10,000.
filing_fee_notes: Tiered by amount sought (§ 50-3-1(a)): $30 ($500 or less), $35 ($500.01-$1,000), $40 ($1,000.01-$2,000), $50 (over $2,000); $30 for non-money relief. § 50-3-1(g) also lists $20 'for filing and trying any civil action'; whether that is charged on top was not confirmed. Sheriff service fee extra; $1 clerk fee for certified mailing (§ 50-3-1(f)).
who_can_sue: Any party may appear in person, by agent, or by attorney; appearance by an agent is not unauthorized practice of law (§ 50-4-4a), so businesses can use non-lawyer agents. Commercial creditors must itemize principal, interest, payments and amount due (§ 50-4-1).
lawyers_notes: Attorneys allowed (§ 50-4-4a).
appeal: Any party may appeal to circuit court within 20 days after judgment (or after a ruling on a motion to set aside), posting bond and paying the circuit court filing fee; the circuit court may allow a late appeal within 90 days for good cause. Bench-trial cases get a new trial (de novo, without jury); jury-trial cases are reviewed on the record (§ 50-5-12). Circuit clerk fee for docketing a civil appeal from magistrate court: $200 (§ 59-1-11).
e_filing_notes: The Judiciary's e-filing page lists Supreme Court, Intermediate Court, Circuit/Family Court and Mass Litigation e-filing only; no magistrate court option found.
fee_waiver_form: Financial affidavit to proceed without prepayment of fees (adopted by the Supreme Court of Appeals under § 59-2-1); available from the clerk
fee_waiver_threshold: 150% of the federal poverty guidelines (yearly net income), set by Supreme Court of Appeals administrative order and updated each year. 2026 table (effective Jan 1, 2026): 1 person $23,475; 2 $31,725; 3 $39,975; 4 $48,225; 5 $56,475; 6 $65,475; 7 $72,975; 8 $81,225. The clerk checks the Financial Affidavit and Application (SCA-C&M201) against the guidelines, and pay stubs or other income proof must be attached.
service_methods: Same manner as in courts of record (§ 50-4-4); the clerk forwards the summons and service fees to the sheriff (§ 50-4-1); certified mail with return receipt is also used (clerk fee in § 50-3-1(f)).

court_name: Small claims (Circuit Court, Wis. Stat. ch. 799)
limit_notes: Money judgments, attachment/garnishment, liens on personal property: $10,000 (rising to $15,000 on January 1, 2027) (Wis. Stat. § 799.01(1)(d)). Personal injury claims, tort claims and third-party complaints: $5,000 (§ 799.01(1)(cr)). Evictions: no limit on rent claimed. Replevin (return of property): $10,000 (rising to $15,000 on January 1, 2027); the courts' page says consumer-credit replevin is allowed where the amount financed is $25,000 or less. Return of earnest money: any amount. Taxing authorities may use small claims up to $10,000.
recent_changes: 2025 Wis. Act 105, effective January 1, 2027: general limit and replevin limit rise from $10,000 to $15,000 (tort/personal injury stays $5,000 in the current statute display). Circuit court fee chart effective November 1, 2026 raised the small claims filing fee from $94.50 to $124.
filing_fee_notes: $124 = $39 filing fee + $61 court support services surcharge + $24 justice information surcharge (fee chart effective Nov. 1, 2026; was $94.50 before). Add $7.50 in Milwaukee County. Add $35 per party if e-filed. Service by mail (where allowed) $7 per defendant plus postage; sheriff/process server fees extra.
who_can_sue: A person may appear on its own or by a Wisconsin attorney; a business acts 'in its own proper person' through a member, agent, or authorized employee. An assignee (e.g., a debt buyer) may not appear through a full-time employee unless that employee is an attorney (Wis. Stat. § 799.06(2)).
lawyers_notes: Attorneys allowed (§ 799.06(2)).
appeal: If a court commissioner decides the case, either party may demand a new trial before a judge within 10 days of an oral decision or 15 days after a written decision is mailed (§ 799.207). Judgments are appealed to the Court of Appeals (§ 799.30) within 45 days of entry if written notice of entry was given within 21 days, otherwise 90 days (§ 808.04(1)); 15 days for eviction appeals (§ 808.04(2)).
e_filing_notes: Circuit court eFiling covers small claims (the fee chart lists the e-filing fee for small claims cases). Attorneys must e-file; self-represented parties may choose to register and e-file (Wis. Stat. § 801.18(3)(b)) or file on paper. Those who register agree to e-file everything the system accepts. The courts' Forms Assistant helps self-represented people prepare forms.
fee_waiver_form: Petition for Waiver of Fees and Costs - Declaration of Indigency (Form CV-410A, 09/24; § 814.29), with order CV-410B: https://wicourts.gov/forms/CV-410A.PDF
fee_waiver_threshold: The court must find poverty and waive fees if the applicant (1) receives means-tested public assistance (e.g. Medicaid/medical assistance, SSI, food stamps, county relief, certain veterans' benefits, AFDC/W-2-type aid), or (2) is represented by a legal services program for indigent people (LSC-funded, public defender, or volunteer programs), or (3) is otherwise unable to pay because of poverty, judged on household size, income, expenses, assets, debts and the federal poverty guidelines (no fixed percentage).
service_methods: Personal or substituted service under ch. 801, or, where a local court rule allows, mail service by the clerk ($7 per defendant; certified mail may be required and is required for evictions); service by mailing and publication if the defendant can't be found (§ 799.12).

court_name: Circuit Court (small claims procedure)
limit_notes: $6,000 exclusive of costs (Wyo. Stat. § 1-21-201). No prejudgment attachment or garnishment (§ 1-21-205). Venue: county where the defendant has an address or where the claim arose (Small Claims Rule 4, eff. Dec. 1, 2021). The Department of Revenue may consolidate tax claims.
filing_fee_notes: $10 filing fee (Rules Governing Small Claims Cases, Rule 3; courts' page). Sheriff or private process server charges a separate fee for each summons served.
who_can_sue: The state, governmental entities, natural persons, corporations, partnerships, associations and other organizations may sue, in person or through authorized employees, with or without an attorney (§ 1-21-202). Plaintiff must swear that demand was made and refused. Assignees not specifically addressed.
lawyers_notes: Lawyers allowed but not required; if one side appears with an attorney, the other side is entitled to a continuance to get one (§ 1-21-202(b)).
appeal: Appeal to district court under the Wyoming Rules of Appellate Procedure, on questions of law only, not sufficiency of the evidence (Small Claims Rule 7). Notice of appeal must be filed with the circuit court clerk within 30 days of the judgment (W.R.A.P. 2.01(a)).
e_filing_notes: Wyoming courts list circuit court eFiling and provide eFile cover sheets for small claims forms SC-01 to SC-06; whether self-represented parties may e-file was not confirmed.
fee_waiver_form: Affidavit of Indigency and Request for Waiver of Fees and Costs (MISC 11) with Order on Request for Waiver of Fees and Costs (MISC 12); instructions MISC 10 (May 2025): https://www.wyocourts.gov/app/uploads/2025/12/MISC-11-Affidavit-of-Indigency-and-Request-for-Waiver-of-Fees-05-25.pdf
fee_waiver_threshold: Judge's discretion: no income test. The applicant gives a detailed sworn financial statement (housing, public assistance, other income, etc.), and a judge decides without having to explain the decision. The instructions say most people do not get fees waived.
service_methods: Sheriff or private process server in person (courts' page); statute also allows the court to serve an in-state defendant by certified mail, return receipt requested (§ 1-21-203). The appearance date must be 12 to 20 days after service (§ 1-21-204).
citation: Wyo. Stat. §§ 1-21-201 to 1-21-205; Wyoming Rules and Forms Governing Small Claims Cases; W.R.A.P. 2.01
